 241: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC002 Every verb resolves exactly one target turn, in this precedence: explicit `requestId` override, else the invocation's bound request, which is refused with `request_ambiguous` while two or more delivered requests are open in the host session (D9); it mutates only that turn; an explicit requestId resolves to exactly one immutable owning MCP session within the validated workspace and agent, and naming a turn of an earlier host session requires its original (MCP `sessionId`, `requestId`) pair, used only by recovery and review backfill (C5); an unknown explicit requestId is refused with `request_unknown`, and a terminal one with `turn_immutable` (except the review and class writes allowed on terminal turns, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004-AC004). A verb whose host session has no delivered request (no write target) is refused with `request_unknown` naming the host session key and writes nothing. A `request_ambiguous` refusal lists each open delivered request's requestId, delivery time, source, and title. [A4 +A8]
 242: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC003 Concurrent edits to two turns from separate processes lose nothing and cross-contaminate nothing. [A4 +A8]
 243: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC004 Failsafe records and fingerprints are namespaced by requestId; replay never targets another turn. A failsafe record without a captured binding (written before the upgrade) is never replayed automatically: it is retained and listed with its path by the stop gate's retained-failsafe warning; a turn in progress in the legacy `current-turn.yaml` at upgrade is listed as a warning by the first SessionStart or Stop and stays addressable by explicit requestId. [A4 +A8]
 244: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC005 Opening, closing, or canceling one turn never changes another turn locally or on the server. [A4 +A8]
 245: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC006 Host-context binding (operator D2): at the start of each verb invocation the plugin resolves the invoking host session's key by the host's locked method (see the host binding table) and binds the invocation to that host session's write target; the binding is written into the invocation's persist and failsafe records and never re-resolved, so a prompt minted after the invocation started never retargets it. On hosts with an arrival bridge, the invocation records the transcript length when it starts and then applies, under `turn-open.lock`, exactly the transcript records that end at or before that length (records appended after it started are left for later invocations), so the binding is the invocation-start snapshot D2 requires, so its binding reflects every delivery recorded before it began. [A4 +A8]
 246: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC007 Interleaving: with R1 delivered and R2 enqueued mid-turn in the same host session, a verb started after R2's mint but before R2's delivery (`absorbed_mid_turn` or `dequeue`) writes to R1; a verb started after R2's delivery without `requestId` is refused with `request_ambiguous` while R1 and R2 are both open (D9); with explicit ids an R1, R2, R1 sequence of writes lands on R1, R2, R1 respectively; once R1 is closed an unqualified verb writes to R2; a withdrawn R2 never becomes a write target; R1 stays in progress throughout. When the verb cannot read its host session key, the live-session rule applies: with exactly one live host session of its agent it binds there with warning `host_session_inferred`; with none or several it is refused (`host_session_unknown`, `host_session_ambiguous`) unless it carries the trusted (MCP `sessionId`, `requestId`) pair of C5 that the server verifies for this workspace and agent; a `requestId` alone is refused the same way; with two concurrent host sessions in one workspace and no keys, zero writes land on the wrong turn. After a prompt's open fails (`turn-open-contended`, `turn-open-failed`, `nonce_source_missing`), unqualified verbs in that host session are refused with `request_unknown` until a later delivery succeeds, so that prompt's work never lands on the earlier turn. A turn the server reports terminal, whichever surface closed it, stops counting as an open delivered request at the next verb or Stop, and a request leaves the open list only when the server confirms its close (a queued, refused, or failed close leaves it open). When the write target is closed while an earlier delivered request is still open, an unqualified verb is refused with `turn_immutable` naming the open request. [A4 +A8]

 475: ### Use cases (new, 9)
 476: 
 477: UC-1 Log each user request as exactly one turn. Actors: Operator, agent host (any of the nine), plugin hooks or tools, model. Precondition: workspace trusted (marker signature and health nonce verified). Basic flow: operator submits a prompt; on a prompt-hook or adapter host the hook classifies it as a user request, takes the turn-open lock, derives the nonce from the event (host binding table), asks the server to mint the requestId (the server opens the turn), and records the token as the host session's write target at once; on a bridge host (claude-code, claude-cowork) the arrival bridge mints from the transcript `enqueue` record (state `queued`) and the request becomes the write target at its `dequeue`, or at an `absorbed_mid_turn` removal (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC009, -AC010); the request enters the stop ledger when it is delivered (at once on prompt-hook and adapter hosts; at its `dequeue` or `absorbed_mid_turn` removal on bridge hosts), never at mint; every verb the model invokes is bound automatically to the host session's write target at invocation start; model closes the turn. Alternate flows: the mint call is retried or replayed and returns the same requestId; a doubly registered hook delivers the event twice and both deliveries get the same requestId; the server is unreachable and a provisional `pending-<nonce>` turn is rebound on drain; an identical prompt sent again later is a new event and opens a second turn; background event is skipped (on a bridge host it keeps its queue position as an unminted system entry, so its `dequeue` delivers nothing); operator sends a message mid-turn, the arrival bridge mints its turn at enqueue without touching the running turn or the write target, the message is delivered (absorbed into the running turn, or dequeued) and from then on, while the earlier request is still open, an unqualified write is refused with `request_ambiguous` (D9) and the model names the requestId of each write; once the earlier request is closed, unqualified writes bind to the delivered request; the operator pulls a queued message back (`popAll`) before delivery, the request is withdrawn, and the stop gate asks the model to fail it; a verb without a host session key in a workspace with two live sessions is refused rather than guessed; a subagent's hooks fire and leave this session's turns unchanged; while two delivered requests are open an unqualified verb is refused with `request_ambiguous` and the model names the requestId (D9); on Copilot with more than one MCP prompt hook registered the hook reports `turn_logging_unsupported` and mints nothing (D11); on a host with no arrival mechanism every session-log verb reports `turn_logging_unsupported` (D6). Realizes FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001, -002, -003, -007, -008; updated FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-001, FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-002, FR-MCP-REPL-010, FR-MCP-TRIAGESTORE-001.

 479: UC-2 Persist session-log writes with truthful receipts. Actors: model, plugin, server. Basic flow: model calls a verb; plugin persists; server returns per-turn outcome; plugin reports persisted only for created/merged. Alternate: target turn is terminal, server reports `skipped_terminal`, plugin reports `persisted:false`, exits non-zero, clears the failsafe; legacy server without outcomes yields `outcomeVerified:false`. Realizes FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004; updated FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-003, FR-MCP-PLUGININT-001.

Basic flow: model records actions/decisions (incl. via `designDecisions`) and closes each turn; Stop hook finds all closed with evidence and passes, clearing the ledger. Alternate: a turn is open (including one whose close the plugin refused for missing model evidence) or fails the completion gate, the Stop hook blocks with the reason and the accepted remedy; a turn closed without evidence by another surface is only warned and never closes turns itself. Realizes FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005, -006; updated FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-005, FR-MCP-CLEARSESSION-001.

 542: ## Wire contracts (documented in P0 before tests)
 543: 
 544: Phase A
 545: - `SessionLogSubmitResult` 201 body adds `turns: [{ requestId, outcome, storedStatus, reason }]`, `outcome` in `created|merged|skipped_terminal` (no `skipped_duplicate`; an identical resubmit is `merged` with reason `no_change`; duplicate requestIds in one submission are applied last-wins with one outcome each). MCP `sessionlog_submit` returns `{ success, id, turns }`. Status code stays 201 (late-hook snapshot protection).
 546: - Plugin receipt on `skipped_terminal`: `code: skipped_terminal`, `persisted: false`, `storedStatus`, `reason`; verb returns false; exit 1; failsafe cleared.
 547: - Hook statuses: new `system-event-skipped`, `turn-open-contended`, `turn-open-failed` (with reason `nonce_source_missing` or the server code); `turn-already-open` when a mint returns `merged` (same nonce).
 548: - Stop gate: blocks `turn_in_progress` (any ledger or registered turn still in_progress), `session_turn_completion_gate` (after S8), failed build after edits (existing), stale session (existing); blocks `turn_withdrawn_unclosed` (a withdrawn queued request still in_progress); warns on exactly the FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC005 list; re-evaluates on every Stop, including `stop_hook_active=true`, blocking again while turns are open and recording `stop_gate_overridden_by_host` if the host stops anyway; passes with `{}` and clears closed entries. Auto-close removed. Block text: `session_turn_stop_gate: <n> turn(s) are not closed correctly:` then one line per turn `<id> (<code>): <remedy>`, then `The stop gate never closes turns for you.`; each turn's remedy accumulates every unmet prerequisite of that turn, in this order: at least one model-authored action, designDecision, or commit (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC002); `requestClass` (after S10); the terminal reviews the completion gate names (after S10, gate order); then the single close call valid for its status: `workflow.sessionlog.failTurn` with reason 'withdrawn before delivery' for a withdrawn request, otherwise `workflow.sessionlog.completeTurn` (or `failTurn` if the work failed), passing requestId <id>. ## Usage Guidance

Use TODO data to refine or confirm the current plan after checking session/task state. Do not start with TODO enumeration when session state already identifies the active task.

## Internal TODO Tracking Toggle

By default, the agent keeps transient checklist state locally and uses MCP TODOs only when the task needs durable workspace TODO tracking. To make MCP TODOs the backing store for durable plan items in a workspace:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T115900Z-todo-internal-enable
  method: workflow.todo.internal.enable
  params: {}
```

To turn it off:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T115901Z-todo-internal-disable
  method: workflow.todo.internal.disable
  params: {}
```

`workflow.todo.internal.status` reports the active state and whether it came from the cached setting, default behavior, or an environment override. An environment-variable override, when set, takes precedence over the cached setting for the current process: set it to `1` to force-enable internal tracking or `0` to force-disable it. The plugin defines the specific override variable name.

```yaml
type: request
payload:
```

The result includes all fields: `implementationTasks`, `description`, `technicalDetails`, `remaining`, `doneSummary`, `dependsOn`, requirement arrays, and timestamps.

30:- Queued-message arrival (operator D5, 2026-10-09: "Arrival bridge"): a message the operator sends while a turn is running is minted when it is enqueued, not when the model later processes it. On hosts that record the enqueue in a transcript (Claude Code), a per-host-session arrival bridge started by the SessionStart hook tails the transcript and follows each queued message through the lifecycle the transcript records. Observed in this workspace's Claude Code transcripts on 2026-10-09: 117 `enqueue`, 79 `dequeue`, 35 `remove` (27 with reason `absorbed_mid_turn`), 2 `popAll`; a normal prompt is `enqueue` then `dequeue` within milliseconds, a mid-turn message is `enqueue` then `remove` with `absorbed_mid_turn` when it is injected into the running turn (for example the operator's mid-turn message beginning "write a global memory with the" was removed with `absorbed_mid_turn` at 2026-10-09T14:35:47.730Z), and `popAll` pulls queued text back into the input box. The bridge mints at `enqueue` (state `queued`); the request becomes `delivered` at `dequeue` (applied by the bridge from the transcript itself; on hosts with a bridge the prompt hook neither mints nor claims) or at `remove` with `absorbed_mid_turn`; it becomes `withdrawn` at `popAll` or a `remove` with any other or no reason. Task notifications and other system events that the host also enqueues are classified and never minted; on bridge hosts they keep their queue position (`kind: system`), so their `dequeue` never delivers a user request.
31:- Hosts without an arrival mechanism (operator D6, 2026-10-09: "Adapters or unsupported"): every host gets an arrival adapter wherever the host offers any mechanism (prompt hook, transcript enqueue record, host-native hook, message-queue event). A host with no arrival mechanism is declared unsupported for turn logging until it gains one: its plugin reports `turn_logging_unsupported` on every session-log verb and writes nothing, and no first-sight minting is used anywhere.
36:- Copilot duplicate deliveries (operator D11, 2026-10-09: "Supported only if single hook"): Copilot gives no stable per-prompt id and separately registered hooks may see different `timestamp` values, so Copilot turn logging is supported only while the plugin's duplicate check proves exactly one MCP prompt hook across all Copilot hook sources; otherwise the Copilot prompt hook reports `turn_logging_unsupported` before any mint, and the condition is a D7 documented limitation until fixed. One Copilot prompt therefore never becomes two turns.
83:- claude-code: nonce: the bridge's `q-` enqueue nonce (the bridge is the only minter, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC009); hook key payload `session_id`; verb key env `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` read at verb start in shell, PowerShell, and hook subprocesses (equals `session_id`; those subprocesses see the updated value after `/clear`); stdio MCP verbs use the live-session rule; payloads carrying `agent_id` are subagent events (system events, no turn); the subagent's own Bash and PowerShell verbs carry the parent's `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` and bind to the parent's write target; stop uses payload `stop_hook_active`. Arrival bridge (D5), the only minter on claude-code (known-good single source of truth: the host transcript is one ordered log written by one producer, so the bridge needs no key shared with the hook, which the host does not provide: Claude Code's `queue-operation` records carry no `promptId` although its user records do): started by SessionStart with the payload `transcript_path`, it applies `queue-operation` lines in file order. Every `enqueue` takes a queue position, so FIFO `dequeue` stays exact. An `enqueue` whose `content` the system-event classifier marks as a system event is added as `{ kind: system, enqueueOffset, enqueueTimestamp, promptSha256, state: queued }` with the root-id envelope and is never minted. An `enqueue` whose `content` the classifier accepts as a user request: mint with nonce `q-` + SHA-256(`session_id` LF the record's starting byte offset in the transcript LF enqueue `timestamp` LF `content`) truncated to 62 hex characters (the offset is unique per record and identical on replay, so two distinct records with equal timestamp and content get two nonces), and add `{ kind: request, requestId, nonce, enqueueOffset, enqueueTimestamp, promptSha256, state: queued, stateOffset, mintedAtUtc }` with the root-id envelope to the queue in `sessions/<key>/turn-state.yaml`. `dequeue` (no content) removes the head of the host session's `queued` entries: a `kind: request` head becomes `delivered` and the write target; a `kind: system` head is removed and delivers nothing. `remove` and `popAll` records that match a `kind: system` entry drop it without a turn. `remove` with reason `absorbed_mid_turn`: the `queued` entry whose `promptSha256` equals the record's `content` hash (both written by the same producer) becomes `delivered` and the write target when exactly one queued entry has that hash. `remove` with any other or no reason: the matching `queued` entry becomes `withdrawn` when exactly one queued entry has that content hash. `popAll`: when, for every content line it carries, the number of lines with that content equals the number of queued entries with that content hash, those entries become `withdrawn`. Fail-closed rule (D6): a `remove` carries `commandUuid` and `deliveryId` (Claude Code 2.1.293), which also appear on the delivered message's `queued_command` attachment, but `enqueue` and `dequeue` carry no key shared with it, so a `remove` that matches two or more queued entries, or a `popAll` that carries fewer lines of a content than there are queued entries with that content, cannot be attributed (a `popAll` whose line count equals the matching entry count withdraws them all, because every candidate is withdrawn). The bridge never guesses: at the first such record it stops before it without advancing `appliedThroughOffset`, sets `turn-state.yaml` `unsupportedSince: { causeOffset, causeOperation, reason: queue_removal_ambiguous }`, and from then on every session-log verb in that host session reports `turn_logging_unsupported` and writes nothing until the session ends. Turns that are open at that moment are left exactly as they are on the server, the stop gate warns `queue_removal_ambiguous` listing them, and the next SessionStart for the agent lists them with their original (MCP `sessionId`, `requestId`) pairs for closing through the trusted recovery flow (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC006). P0.2 records the `remove` identity fields; the bridge never uses them to pair with an `enqueue`. Only `queue-operation` lines are arrival records; every other record type is ignored by design. A `queue-operation` with an unknown operation or a missing required field is never skipped: the bridge stops before it without advancing `appliedThroughOffset`, records warning `arrival_bridge_format_unrecognized`, and the host session reports `turn_logging_unsupported` on every session-log verb (D6) until a verified adapter handles that shape. Each record's state change and the advance of `appliedThroughOffset` past it are one atomic replace of `turn-state.yaml` (temp file, flush, rename, under `turn-open.lock`); records that start below `appliedThroughOffset` are skipped, so a restart never re-applies a record; the server mint for `enqueue` happens before that replace and is idempotent (same nonce, `merged`). Records are applied by whichever process holds `turn-open.lock`: the bridge, or a session-log verb, which first records the transcript length at the moment the invocation starts and, after taking the lock, applies every pending record that ends at or before that length, never a record appended later, before it binds (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC006), so a verb started after a `dequeue` line was written binds to that request, and a `dequeue` appended after the verb started never retargets it (D2). The prompt hook on claude-code and claude-cowork neither mints nor claims; it classifies system events and starts no turn. P0.2 verifies that every user prompt (in each prompt form of FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC009) produces an `enqueue` record and that `dequeue` always takes the head; if either fails, claude-code is `turn_logging_unsupported` (D6) until an adapter with a traceable key exists, recorded in the feature matrix.

One message yields exactly one mint for every prompt form P0.2 captures (plain, slash command, attachment or image, image-only, multi-line CRLF, non-ASCII, at least 1 MiB), and two messages with equal text yield two mints. A pid file naming a dead or foreign process does not prevent a bridge start; a host session ended by the idle rule is live again at its next mint or keyed verb; a resumed or forked transcript mints nothing for queue records written before that host session's SessionStart; a transcript shorter than `appliedThroughOffset` is reported with `arrival_bridge_format_unrecognized`, changes nothing, and the host session reports `turn_logging_unsupported` until the bridge restarts on a valid transcript (fail closed, like an unknown record shape); the bridge restarts from SessionStart after `/clear` and resume and stops at SessionEnd. 202:- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC010 Queue lifecycle: a `queued` request becomes `delivered` (and the host session's write target) at `dequeue` (the head of the queue) or at `remove` with reason `absorbed_mid_turn`, and becomes `withdrawn` at a `popAll` or a `remove` with any other or no reason; minting never moves the write target; a withdrawn request stays `in_progress` on the server until the model closes it (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC009). A record that cannot be attributed to exactly one queued entry (equal content with no shared key: a `remove` matching two or more entries, or a `popAll` carrying fewer lines of a content than there are matching entries) is never guessed: the host session fails closed under D6 (the bridge stops before the record, `unsupportedSince` is recorded, every session-log verb in that host session reports `turn_logging_unsupported` and writes nothing until it ends, and its open turns are listed with their pairs at the next SessionStart); a `popAll` whose line count equals the matching entry count withdraws them all. 477:UC-1 Log each user request as exactly one turn. Actors: Operator, agent host (any of the nine), plugin hooks or tools, model. 78: Host binding table (locks the D1 nonce source, the D5 arrival source, and the D2 host session key per host; every turn token is still minted by the server). Rules common to all hosts:
79: - Nonce: computed from the event itself, never from the hook process, so every delivery of one event yields the same nonce; a value outside `^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,64}$` is replaced by the 64 lowercase hex characters of its SHA-256.
80: - Host session key: read from the verb's own invocation context as listed per host. Long-lived processes (stdio MCP servers, the arrival bridge itself) never trust a key captured at spawn time, because a host may change the session in place (Claude Code `/clear`; resume without an explicit id keeps the startup id in long-lived subprocesses per the Claude Code env-var reference); they resolve the key per call by the live-session rule.
81: - Queued-message arrival on every host (D5, D6): P0.2 records, per host, whether a message sent while a turn is running reaches an arrival mechanism at enqueue. Where the prompt event itself fires at enqueue, it is the arrival mechanism; where it fires only at processing time, the host's transcript or queue event is used through an arrival adapter with the same `queued`/`delivered`/`withdrawn` lifecycle as the Claude Code bridge; where neither exists, the host is unsupported for turn logging (`turn_logging_unsupported`).
82: - Live-session rule (D2 fallback): a host session is live from its first mint until its session-end event (Claude Code `SessionEnd`, including reason `clear`; Codex `SessionEnd`; Copilot session end; cline-v2 and opencode session close) marks `sessions/<key>/ended.yaml`, or until 12 hours without a mint or verb. A verb without its own key binds to the single live session of its agent in the workspace (`host_session_inferred`), and is refused with `host_session_unknown` (none live) or `host_session_ambiguous` (several live) unless it passes the trusted (MCP `sessionId`, `requestId`) pair of C5.

Arrival bridge (D5), the only minter on claude-code (known-good single source of truth: the host transcript is one ordered log written by one producer, so the bridge needs no key shared with the hook, which the host does not provide: Claude Code's `queue-operation` records carry no `promptId` although its user records do): started by SessionStart with the payload `transcript_path`, it applies `queue-operation` lines in file order. Every `enqueue` takes a queue position, so FIFO `dequeue` stays exact. An `enqueue` whose `content` the system-event classifier marks as a system event is added as `{ kind: system, enqueueOffset, enqueueTimestamp, promptSha256, state: queued }` with the root-id envelope and is never minted. An `enqueue` whose `content` the classifier accepts as a user request: mint with nonce `q-` + SHA-256(`session_id` LF the record's starting byte offset in the transcript LF enqueue `timestamp` LF `content`) truncated to 62 hex characters (the offset is unique per record and identical on replay, so two distinct records with equal timestamp and content get two nonces), and add `{ kind: request, requestId, nonce, enqueueOffset, enqueueTimestamp, promptSha256, state: queued, stateOffset, mintedAtUtc }` with the root-id envelope to the queue in `sessions/<key>/turn-state.yaml`. `dequeue` (no content) removes the head of the host session's `queued` entries: a `kind: request` head becomes `delivered` and the write target; a `kind: system` head is removed and delivers nothing. `remove` and `popAll` records that match a `kind: system` entry drop it without a turn. `remove` with reason `absorbed_mid_turn`: the `queued` entry whose `promptSha256` equals the record's `content` hash (both written by the same producer) becomes `delivered` and the write target when exactly one queued entry has that hash. `remove` with any other or no reason: the matching `queued` entry becomes `withdrawn` when exactly one queued entry has that content hash. `popAll`: when, for every content line it carries, the number of lines with that content equals the number of queued entries with that content hash, those entries become `withdrawn`. Fail-closed rule (D6): a `remove` carries `commandUuid` and `deliveryId` (Claude Code 2.1.293), which also appear on the delivered message's `queued_command` attachment, but `enqueue` and `dequeue` carry no key shared with it, so a `remove` that matches two or more queued entries, or a `popAll` that carries fewer lines of a content than there are queued entries with that content, cannot be attributed (a `popAll` whose line count equals the matching entry count withdraws them all, because every candidate is withdrawn). The bridge never guesses: at the first such record it stops before it without advancing `appliedThroughOffset`, sets `turn-state.yaml` `unsupportedSince: { causeOffset, causeOperation, reason: queue_removal_ambiguous }`, and from then on every session-log verb in that host session reports `turn_logging_unsupported` and writes nothing until the session ends. P0.2 records the `remove` identity fields; the bridge never uses them to pair with an `enqueue`. Only `queue-operation` lines are arrival records; every other record type is ignored by design. A `queue-operation` with an unknown operation or a missing required field is never skipped: the bridge stops before it without advancing `appliedThroughOffset`, records warning `arrival_bridge_format_unrecognized`, and the host session reports `turn_logging_unsupported` on every session-log verb (D6) until a verified adapter handles that shape. 200: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC008 When the server is unreachable at ingress, the hook persists a failsafe mint record carrying its nonce and opens a provisional local turn `pending-<nonce>`; on failsafe drain the server mints idempotently from the nonce and the plugin rebinds the provisional turn and every write bound to it to the minted requestId, in original order. Either id resolves to the same turn; a crash at any point during the rebind loses no write and creates no second turn; a committed pending-to-minted alias stays discoverable and is reapplied until every consumer of it (including an audit outbox) durably acknowledges it, and duplicate delivery or application is harmless (C2). With two or more consumers, an alias acknowledged by one stays discoverable to the others; replay to a consumer stops only after that consumer durably acknowledges, and stops entirely once all have. No server turn ever has a `pending-` requestId: a write captured under a pending id and sent after the alias is sent under the minted id, and the writes of one turn reach the server in their original order even when a close of that turn was made while earlier writes waited in the failsafe. A mint that the server or REPL does not support (missing route or verb, as on a server older than A1) is handled like an outage (failsafe retained, turn stays `pending-<nonce>`, retried at a later drain); a mint refused for a final reason (404 session not open, 400 validation) reports `turn-open-failed` with the server code, keeps its failsafe record marked final and not retried, invents no requestId, and the stop gate warns naming the prompt.
